title: Localization Contrast As a Fundamental Limit of Radiative Quantum Efficiency
authors: Arsineh Apelian, Tanay Tak, Xuance Jiang, Tsung-Yin Tsai, James S. Speck, Vojtech Vlcek
abstract: Disorder can localize valence- and conduction-band states to different degrees, yet whether such localization contrast has observable consequences remains poorly understood. Here, we show that localization contrast strongly impacts competing carrier-recombination channels. We illustrate this behavior in random In$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N alloys. Increasing the In content from $x=13.5\%$ to $x=22\%$ progressively localizes the valence-band maximum state while leaving the conduction-band minimum state comparatively delocalized. This contrasting localization decreases the interband optical momentum matrix element underlying radiative recombination. For Auger-Meitner recombination, however, localization alone does not determine the coupling; atomic-scale disorder also breaks primitive-cell translational symmetry and modifies the momentum-space and phase structure of the states. This generates additional low-$Q$ components and enhances the Auger coupling by more than five orders of magnitude relative to pristine GaN. Thus, we provide a microscopic explanation for the competing trends in radiative and Auger recombination. More broadly, our results establish localization contrast as a mechanism through which disorder can control optical and carrier-carrier interactions in semiconductors.
summary: This paper demonstrates that disorder in semiconductor alloys like InGaN creates a 'localization contrast' between valence and conduction bands. This contrast suppresses the desirable radiative recombination pathway but, counterintuitively, dramatically enhances the non-radiative Auger recombination pathway. The findings establish localization contrast as a key mechanism controlling optical and carrier-carrier interactions in disordered semiconductors.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the 'localization contrast'—the differing degrees of localization between valence and conduction band states due to disorder—affects competing carrier recombination channels in semiconductors.
main_result: Localization contrast suppresses radiative recombination by reducing the interband optical momentum matrix element, but it dramatically enhances Auger recombination by breaking translational symmetry and generating low-Q components.
method: The study uses first-principles calculations on random supercells to calculate recombination rates via momentum and Coulomb matrix elements, quantifying localization using the Participation Ratio (PR).
model_or_system: The system modeled is random In_xGa_{1-x}N alloys, relevant for LEDs. The analysis compares radiative recombination (governed by the momentum matrix element) against Auger-Meitner recombination (governed by Coulomb interactions).
key_observables: Localization Contrast ($\langle 	ext{PR}_{	ext{VBM}} / 	ext{PR}_{	ext{CBM}} angle$), Radiative Strength ($\langle S_{	ext{rad}} angle$), and Auger Recombination Strength ($\langle S_{	ext{Auger}} angle$).
important_parameters: In content ($x$), disorder strength, and the ratio of localization between VBM and CBM.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field treatments using single-particle orbitals and assumes that the contrasting response of the momentum and Coulomb operators to disorder dictates the recombination efficiency.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the localization contrast ratio in InGaN (decreasing) versus InGaAs (constant). Figure 2 shows the reduction in radiative strength with In content, while Figure 3 and 4 detail the large enhancement of Auger strength due to disorder.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the concept of localization contrast in InGaN. It then analyzes the effect of this contrast on radiative recombination, showing suppression. Subsequently, it analyzes Auger recombination, demonstrating that disorder enhances this channel far more significantly than the radiative channel.
why_interesting: The work provides a quantitative, microscopic link between structural disorder (localization contrast) and the competition between fundamental optical processes (radiative vs. Auger), which is crucial for understanding efficiency droop in modern optoelectronic devices.

The ratio decreases with In content in InGaN, indicating that the valence edge localizes relative to the conduction edge but is constant in InGaAs over the range sampled. Error bars are standard deviations over 15 random configurations per composition for InGaN and 5 for InGaAs.

Figure 1 shows the resulting configurationally aver- aged localization ratio ⟨PRVBM/PRCBM⟩. Our results demonstrate that alloy disorder reduces the PR of both band edges relative to pristine GaN, but acts far more strongly on the valence edge. At 13.5% In, the PRVBM and PRCBM are reduced by 55% and 19%, respectively, while at 22% In the reductions increase to 63% and 22%. The localization ratio (black curve) therefore decreases substantially with In content. A natural question is whether this behavior is common to other widely used III–V alloys or is instead a distinc- tive feature of the nitrides.
